checkedAgainst: Regression, deadline and paired month fixtures; engineering policy, not population parameters. Heap cap reuses the core profiling command; job deadlines include five minutes for dependency setup. Profile parsing is bounded separately from retained summaries. Measured span: a whole year of the two-level world with the economy (audit 4, Oct 12), not a month of the full population.
semiSpaceReason: V8 young-generation size for the play server and every guarded run (core-year-speed-remaining, Oct 15): a played year allocates a great many short-lived records, and the default 16 MiB young generation spends about 16% of the year collecting. Measured on a 4-core cloud container, one process at a time, same cash to the cent: Garden City, Idaho (seed speed-gc-1) 118.5 s to 101.7 s; Exeter, New Hampshire (seed speed-ex-1) 134.3 s to 116.5 s at 64 MiB, 128.1 s at 32 MiB and 118.9 s at 128 MiB. Keep desktop/play-api-client.mjs in step.
memoryCeilingsReason: MEMORY-FLAT (docs/packages/MEMORY-FLAT.md): a two-level played world should cost tens of megabytes, as The Political Process keeps statistics per place and compact records per official. Heap after a forced collection, bookkeeping off: after importing the engine (before any town), after the opening, and growth a month from the end of the first month (whose one-time tables are excluded) to the end of the run. Starting numbers set by the package; TUNABLE against the played-world test's measured towns.
goldenBudgetReason: Measured on a four-core container: the played-world year (M0-13) takes 168 s alone and about 6 minutes on GitHub's runner, so it runs as its own job under longRunningMilliseconds. Measured Nov 14 (GitHub's runner, run 43618870786): the first fourteen accepted specs took 34.1, 14.0, 21.0, 10.5, 19.9, 49.6, 1.1, 0.2, 3.1, 16.6, 79.5, 22.3, 19.2 and 15.0 s, 306 s together, which left M2-06 144 s of the 450 s. The accepted specs after them took, alone in this container, M2-07 36 s, M2-08 17 s, M2-04 27 s, M2-09 47 s and M3-09 32 s, so the quick job's accepted specs come to about 480 s against the 450 s budget with a container's times, which is not yet measured on GitHub's runner. Measured Nov 14 at the pinned town (Ridgewood, New Jersey): a 17.6 s build and about 0.09 s per played day, so the economy check's 120 days take 37 s in the quick job (as M1-02Q) and its two years, 730 days, about 86 s, run in the long job as M1-02 with every assertion kept
timeBudgetReason: A large drawn town's year can take five to six minutes a run on GitHub's runner (Derry, New Hampshire, drawn for PR 5871: ten runs did not fit performanceMilliseconds), and about 11 on a four-core container. Each warmup plays warmupDays, and from the warmups' time a game day and their fixed time (process start, opening, modules) the guard measures the longest span up to measuredDays that fits three pairs and two profiles, so a town whose month fits compares three alternating pairs; warmupDays is also the shortest span, and a town too slow for even that measures as many pairs as fit. Base and head alternate; after the first measured pair another starts only while the last pair's time times runTimeMargin fits the time left, and each profile only while its last run's time times profileTimeMargin does, so a large town measures fewer pairs instead of failing on time. The margins cover the run-to-run spread of a year (a few percent) plus process start and receipt parsing.
